source.name: Institute for Government, Public Services Performance Tracker 2026 (cross-service analysis, Oct 2026; NHS report, Nov 2026)

note: Ratings and facts summarised from the IfG reports; read the originals for method and caveats.

services.why: Many more salaried GPs and better access and satisfaction, but GP partner numbers keep falling and children wait far longer for community care than in 2024.
Elective care improving but on course to miss the 2029 target by a wide margin; A&E and diagnostics near 2024 levels; structural reorganisation is a drag.
Funding formula redesigned towards deprived areas and SEND deficit pressure eased, but more councils rely on one-off fixes; funding per person still about 14% below 2010-11 in real terms by 2028-29.
Tighter overseas recruitment may store up workforce shortages; reforms unlikely to bite before 2029.
Clear reform vision, but changes are upstream and slow, and compete for council capacity.
Absence falling from record highs and teacher recruitment on track; SEND reform details unclear and unlikely to change much before 2030.
More neighbourhood officers and PCSOs; continued progress depends on further funding.
More activity and capacity, but not enough to meet demand; backlogs will take years to fall.
Capacity freed up and some progress on violence and conditions, at risk from later policy changes.

nhs_facts: Elective waiting list fell by about 250,000 cases (3.3%) between June 2024 and August 2026; the March 2026 target was met but performance has since worsened.
IfG central estimate: 79% of elective cases waiting under 18 weeks by March 2029 against a 92% target.
Long A&E waits barely moved: 10.3% waited over 12 hours in the year before July 2024, 10.2% in the latest year.
Hospitals cut more than 12,000 non-clinical staff (-1.6%) since March 2025, partly to reach financial balance.
Salaried GPs up almost a third (32.9%, about 3,500 more) since June 2024, but GP partners down 945 (-5.9%).
27.0% of children wait more than a year for community care, up from 14.4% in mid-2024.
Only 29.5% of DHSC civil servants agreed senior leaders had a clear vision in 2025 (49.9% across the civil service).
Hospital clinical workforce grew faster (5.2%) than primary and community clinical workforce (4.0%), June 2024 to June 2026, despite the aim to shift care into the community.
NHS England is being abolished and integrated care boards reorganised, with 50% headcount cuts targeted in those organisations.
